devin: quick RFC follow-up: propose 'elastic-credit smoothing' instead of fixed windows. want quick gut-check on router-admission API and operator safety.
anya: TLDR of benefit? fewer sudden throttles during microbursts?
kevin: yes, smoother absorb + lower p95 tail, but need low-cost convergence across routers.
maria: suggestion: admission keeps per-tenant float credit with exponential decay; routers cache last_seen and apply local subtracts for grants. periodic reconcile to central checkpoint.
lukas: how do we avoid double-grant when two routers grant simultaneously between reconciles?
kevin: add a tiny per-grant id and per-router delta-log. merge = base_decayed + sum(unique_deltas). make deltas compact by batching per-100ms.
anya: delta-log compaction is key. also add 'speculative_grant_limit' so routers can do tiny low-latency grants without blowing budgets.
maria: operator needs: authoritative snapshot endpoint, fast-reset flag, and an audit event when credit drops under threshold for VIP tenants.
devin: API sketch: router -> admission: {tenant, want_units, router_id} response: {granted, remaining_credit, epoch, decay_ms, speculative_limit}. keep it minimal.
lukas: telemetry: measure "credit_divergence_pct" (sample routers pairwise) and alert if >4% for >90s.
kevin: rollout: 1) log-only responses for 2w 2) shadow mode on 10% routers 3) canary 1% live 4) ramp with rollback triggers: p95 latency +5% or unexpected_throttle_rate +0.4%.
anya: i'll add simulator job with sustained + spike traffic and a long-tail client mix.
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-8420 for runbook + alerts (https://tracker/redwood/INFRA-8420).
